note: Rule 24 / Rule 30(d) ledger — every audit that ran, when, on what class of work, and what it found. Gate-blocks: a phase or gate cannot advance until its required audits ran or are deferred with a reason. Check it with: node ~/.claude/skills/bob/../scripts/audit-ledger-check.mjs docs/audit-ledger.json (add --streaks for the five-clean-in-a-row count).

fields.audit: what was audited, in one line — the milestone, phase or change (name the PR or commit if there is one).
fields.tier: 1, 2 or 3 per the definition of done (Rule 30(a): 1 = numbers or data someone acts on).
fields.class_of_work: exactly one value from class_of_work_vocabulary; free-text nuance goes in class_of_work_detail.
fields.material_found: integer: Material findings raised across every round of this audit, including ones fixed before merge.
fields.material_remaining: integer: Material findings still open when the entry was written (all fixed = 0). Never more than material_found.
fields.minor: integer: Minor findings (fix if cheap, else log with a revisit trigger).
fields.auditor_context: who audited: 'fresh subagent', 'new session', 'human' — never the context that built the work (Rule 30(b)).
fields.rounds: optional integer: audit rounds run. 0 means no audit actually ran (the entry records a skip), and the streak walk skips it.
fields.coverage: optional object {planned, covered, deferred, blocked, out_of_scope}: unit counts from the coverage record (audit-lenses/_evidence-accounting.md §1), so 'five clean audits' means five COVERED audits, not five quiet ones.
fields.zero_finding_rerun: optional: when material_found is 0, the different angle the audit was re-run from (Rule 30(f)), or why it was not.
fields.at_decision: optional: the decision-log id this audit sits at (D-nnn); used to order same-day entries.
fields.unrecorded: only for entries migrated in from an older ledger: names the fields left null because the old entry does not state them. New entries may not use null.
fields.count_note: optional: how a migrated count was read from the old entry's own text.

class_of_work_vocabulary.docs-planning: specs, plans, decisions and other documents; no runtime change
class_of_work_vocabulary.data-pipeline: moving data in and through the system: imports, sync jobs, transformations, deduplication
class_of_work_vocabulary.data-repair: one-off corrections to stored production data, and their verification
class_of_work_vocabulary.calculations: any logic that produces a number or a verdict someone acts on: pricing, totals, scores, rankings
class_of_work_vocabulary.outputs: what users receive: pages, exports, reports, notifications and emails
class_of_work_vocabulary.ops-ci: CI, scheduled jobs, locks, run records, monitoring and alerting
class_of_work_vocabulary.platform: auth, billing/payments, security, model access, infrastructure
class_of_work_vocabulary.mixed: one entry covering several changes of different classes; counted in no class streak

format.vocabulary_rule: Edit the vocabulary to fit the project, but keep it small and fixed: 3 to 12 values, 'mixed' always present. A new free-text class per entry is how a ledger stops being countable.
format.streak_rule: Per class, walk entries newest first (ordered by ran, then decision number, then position). Tier 2/3 entries and entries with rounds = 0 (no audit ran) are skipped. A Tier-1 entry with material_found = 0 extends the streak; anything else stops it — including material_found null and tier null, because an unrecorded count is not evidence of a clean audit. Five → propose (never apply) demoting that class to Tier 2.
